utterances.text: Yes. The road should stay open because they told us there could be some transport moving to Srebrenica, and from Srebrenica to Potocari. Well, we collected the people at the point and we stayed there, patrolling during the night. The Serbs, they left. Some of them came back during the night and they were taking our arms and also our vests and helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Can you describe in what way they did that.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, they joined -- they formed groups of three or four men, and they walked up to a UN soldier and told him to give away his weapon, his bulletproof vest, his helmet, and his equipment, and when he refused that, he was forced to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: At gunpoint?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Me personally at gunpoint, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: How many of your soldiers did lose their equipment in this way?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know. Many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Many out of these 30, 40 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The majority?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: The majority, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: That went on during the night.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning of the night. Later on that night they disappeared, and I didn't know where they went. We were alone with these people and then they were very, very quiet. Well, we kept on patrolling during the night -- well, helping some sick people, also again wounded people who still asked for doctors, for medical help, and we had a doctor outside our position -- well, till morning came.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Okay. Then we arrive at the 13th of July. I will now ask you to tell the Court what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: On the 13th, well, we put down four APCs on the road to make some of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: "APCs" stands for?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Armoured personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Armoured personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Armoured, yes. Sorry. To make some of them an artificial gate so we could guide the people in a better way. Then at approximately 700 hours the buses arrived, and half an hour later the Serbs arrived. Then there were more and more troops coming down to our position, and when --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Again, an estimation, if you can. How many troops?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: At least 50, 60 of them. Then they started again to pull away my men and to put the people inside of the buses and the trucks, and that carried on during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Any attacks on you or your personnel during the day?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Shooting?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Nothing?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: We heard some shooting on the west side of the compound coming from houses and that kind of thing. But not on my position, there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Did this separation type of handling, this thing, did that go on even this day? Did they separate men from the rest of their families, or was that done only on the first day?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, it still went on that day. For example, we saw a 19-year-old boy being separated from his family and, well, we protested against it, and the Serbian soldier, he was impressed and let the boy go to the buses. But they carried on separating the men, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: That went on on the 13th of July, all day?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: From what I've seen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: When was the place emptied of refugees or everybody evacuated? When was that?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I will have to look it up. One moment, please. It was on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: What time of the day; can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, it would be approximately at 1800 hours. I had to do my report at the compound and get some food and a few hours of sleep, two hours, and that was at 1600 hours. When I reported to duty in the operations room, that was at 1830, I was told that it wasn't necessary any more because all the people had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: All of them?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: All of them had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Even the people who were in the compound?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, except the wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Except the wounded people?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: They left the wounded people. What about the men who were separated? Were they still around or were they gone also?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: They were also gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Did you see them go?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, because I was in the compound sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Did you see when the people were taken from that compound into the buses?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You didn't see that. Did you see or hear any violence during the 13th? Was there any shooting then or other kinds of violence?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, not in person. We heard several single shots, like I told you before. We did hear some rumours; that was on the 12th of July, while I was reporting at the compound. We heard some rumours from people inside the compound that there was a place where they had seen eight or nine bodies laying down on the ground. On the 13th of July, two colleagues of mine and I investigated that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Was that in the vicinity of the compound -- outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, it was approximately -- well, 500 metres away from the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: What did you find?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: When we came down to that place, we saw nine bodies laying in a field, near to a river. We went up to that location and we took pictures. We didn't actually investigate the bodies, but we saw seven of them lying down on the ground, with their face down to the ground. Two of them were lying on their sides, their backs. They had -- well, the seven of them had a shot in the back, in the middle of the back. We took pictures, and we also found some papers. But the bodies, they were just in civilian clothes, and from what I could see and make of it, they were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You did these findings on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Did you hear some shooting you could relate to that incident, to these people's death?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, I only heard the several single shots during the day. That's only what I have heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Did you see other killed people around?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that was in the morning. One man hanged himself on the ceiling of a small building, and he was already dead when we released him from the rope.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Any other incidents of that kind?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: So by the evening of the 13th, the place was empty, there were no refugees any more.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Outside of the compound, no. Inside also, no, except the wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The wounded people. Did you see General Mladic more than these times on the 12th that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. During the night on the 12th and on the 13th, during that night I saw him passing by our position, sitting in a jeep. He moved up to Srebrenica, and later on that night he moved back towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: So you saw him twice during that night.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You saw him twice during that night?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: But he didn't stop?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You didn't talk to him?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: He just drove on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Okay. Then when only the wounded people were left, what happened then? What did you do in the coming days?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, for me personally, I picked up my job again as a logistics officers, doing the things requested and waiting for us to leave the enclave. We were making preparations for leaving the enclave because we didn't know if we could leave with all our equipment or just by taking our personal belongings and then leave the compound. So I took up my old job.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: As a logistics officer, you can certainly tell us, how much equipment did you lose during these days?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact numbers and figures. We lost weapons; we did lose some jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: How many jeeps?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Can you make an estimation?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You can't.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: APCs, we lost APCs, and we lost, well, equipment, soldiers' equipment, bulletproof vests, and helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: When did you leave? When did the battalion leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: It was on the 21st, on Friday, July.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The week after.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: The week after that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have concluded my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ostberg. Fellow Judges, you have questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Lieutenant Koster, you talk of 15.000 people coming from Srebrenica to Potocari looking for help. Mostly, you said, they were women and children and elderly people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Were you expecting this exodus from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Were you in Potocari, you and your team, expecting this exodus from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We were outside there to receive the refugees, yes, and we could expect that refugees should come to our position. That's why we were posted outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Were you prepared for receiving them?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No. Just being there, being posted there, and doing the best we can. We didn't have the equipment, medical equipment, or even enough food to receive them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Had you, your team, asked for help to your superiors or to the superior command of NATO or UNPROFOR to face this emergency?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Did you receive any additional support for help before or after the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: What happened with these people, women, children, elderly, wounded people, when the Bosnian Serb soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Sorry. You're only talking now about the wounded people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: About the women, children, elderly people in Potocari, coming from Srebrenica, when the Serb soldiers arrived.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, they were afraid and they were not harmed or anything by the Serbian people, from what I could see, outside the compound. Well, later on, during the periods we were outside, they were put inside the buses and evacuated from my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Did you hear about massacres committed by Serb soldiers against Muslims in and around Srebrenica, Potocari, Bratunac at that time?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I only learned on the Wednesday that there was a position -- there was a rumour about eight or nine bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: After those days, had you heard about massacres committed?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, only when I returned, in the news.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Did Colonel Karremans, or anyone else, say no to General Mladic when he ordered the evacuation of the refugees?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I do not know that because they already started it when I was reporting it. So the situation was completely taken out of our hands outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: But the refugees were under your support, under the UN support, under protection.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: So did you or your superior try to avoid that the refugees were taken out?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: It was impossible to do because we were outnumbered. We were pulled away, and then the Serbs, they pushed the people and shouted at the people to go to the buses now, to get inside these buses. So being outnumbered, we couldn't do anything at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Lieutenant Koster, you just said that you were outnumbered, completely outnumbered. In fact, you were in a state of helplessness, completely.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were you at any moment threatened?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: In person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No, the whole group, in your capacity, you and your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No. We were just told to cooperate, that that would be the best for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, "best for us" means that something could be worst; if there is something best, then something can be worst. You mentioned that Mladic himself told you, he told you you'd better cooperate, you are right, and then he told you, "You will see what is going to happen." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mladic, among his statements, he told you, "You are going to see what will happen." You mentioned that from your notes.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I still don't understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What did Mladic tell you?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, he told me that, and later on he told me that he was going to evacuate the people of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Then you mentioned that you saw them separate men of fighting age from the others.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you protest or anything?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You did. What was the reaction to your protest?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, sometimes they let the men go with their families and their wives. Well, at the places we were -- we couldn't protest where we were not located, so we couldn't do a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did they pick them just at random, or did they have a list in their hands?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, just at random.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Because there was a list of 200-and-something people which nobody knew if it was given to them or not. Do you have any idea about that?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I know about that list, yes, and that was on the compound -- at the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: That list was made just to make sure and to inform the Serbs that we were watching them and keeping things under control about what they were going to do with the men, and by that list we were also protecting them. So we were checking them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: This list was made by your men, by the officers?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: It was made by a committee of the refugees inside the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And given to you?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, not to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean to your --

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: My commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: From what I know, it was not given to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You don't know if it was given to the Serbs or not.

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: From what I know, it was not given to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was not. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lieutenant, on the basis of what we've heard, apparently there's some vehicles from the battalion that escorted the jeeps -- some jeeps that escorted the vehicles, so you did have some jeeps that went along with the convoys. Now, I take it that those jeeps came back, at least some of them came back, so you had a chance to see some of your men before you left the compound. What did your men tell you about what happened, and were they aware of the events?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: I only learnt about that when we left the enclave. Before that I was constantly being outside, until the 13th, and I didn't know what was going on during these escorts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the jeeps that were doing the escorting did not leave Potocari?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Some of them were already taken away at our main gate, and, well, that's what they told me while I was doing my reports. Well, at least one of them made it through, and that was the first transport. But that is something I learned later, when I left the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When soldiers came back, because there was a gathering before you left the enclave, what did people say to one another? What did the soldiers say there? Did anybody tell you anything? Did they know anything?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing was said?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't say anything about what they might have seen? They didn't see anything?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't speaking to them. I was too busy at that time doing my job as a logistics officer so I don't know anything about that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. You got together on a regular basis with the reports about the meetings with General Mladic, or was there a compartmentalisation between the different levels of command?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: Can the interpreter repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have any input about the meetings with General Mladic, or was there no information trickling down at the various levels?

utterances.speaker: LIEUTENANT KOSTER
utterances.text: No, I didn't know what was going on. I didn't know the exact details of the meetings with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Ostberg, we have no further questions for the witness so we could have the usher show the witness out. Lieutenant, the Tribunal would like to thank you for your testimony which you provided on behalf of the Prosecution. Then the Prosecution can show in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. That's all you have to offer us today, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn till tomorrow, at 9.30. Thank you.
